        ### Question
        Indicate which serum biochemical profile is suggestive of rickets due to vitamin D deficiency in a 5-month-old infant:

        ### Options

opb. Normal calcium; low phosphate; Normal FA; Normal PTH; 25 OH vitamin D low.
opc. Low calcium; high phosphate; FA elevated; Normal PTH; 25 OH vitamin D low.
opd. Normal calcium; normal phosphate; FA elevated; Elevated PTH; 25 OH vitamin D low.

### Reasoning Chains per Option:
CHAIN: "Vitamin D deficiency" -> "decreased intestinal absorption of calcium" -> "normal serum calcium levels" -> "normal serum phosphate levels" -> "normal alkaline phosphatase levels" -> "elevated parathyroid hormone" -> "low 25 OH vitamin D" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Vitamin D deficiency" -> "increased bone resorption" -> "low serum calcium" -> "high serum phosphate" -> "elevated alkaline phosphatase" -> "normal parathyroid hormone" -> "low 25 OH vitamin D" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Vitamin D deficiency" -> "increased parathyroid hormone secretion" -> "normal serum calcium" -> "low serum phosphate" -> "normal alkaline phosphatase" -> "low 25 OH vitamin D" -> 80%
CHAIN: "Vitamin D deficiency" -> "increased bone turnover" -> "normal serum calcium" -> "normal phosphate" -> "elevated alkaline phosphatase" -> "elevated parathyroid hormone" -> "low 25 OH vitamin D" -> 75%
